TITLE::New Birth and Life Through the Son

Nicodemus visits Jesus at night and hears that people must be born again, born of water and the Spirit, to enter the kingdom of God. Jesus says the Son of Man must be lifted up so believers may have eternal life. God sent His Son to save the world out of love, but those who reject Him stand condemned and prefer darkness to light. John denies being the Christ and rejoices that Jesus gains followers while his own role grows smaller. The Son is above all, with eternal life for believers, while God's wrath remains on those who reject Him.

Themes: Night visit of Nicodemus · Born anew · Water and Spirit · Son of Man lifted up · God’s love for the world · Light and darkness · John’s humility · Eternal life and wrath

Key People: Nicodemus · Jesus · John · John’s disciples · Moses

Key Places: Judea

Key Points:
• Jesus distinguishes birth from flesh from being born again through the Spirit when He speaks to Nicodemus.
• Jesus says believers receive eternal life through the Son of Man being lifted up.
• God sends His Son to save, but unbelief brings condemnation as people prefer darkness to light.
• John rejoices that Jesus gains followers and accepts that his own importance must decrease.
• The Son has authority from the Father, and rejecting Him leaves a person under God's wrath.

Supporting Verses: John 3:1-10 · John 3:13-15 · John 3:16-21 · John 3:22-30 · John 3:31-36
